task_summary: Matching-theory undersampling: methods, KEEL benchmark study, LaTeX manuscript

steps.title: Install dependencies and freeze versions
steps.description: Install the PyPI extras into the imbml environment (KEEL data package, matching library for reference solvers, scikit-posthocs, baycomp, complexity-measure package) and save a frozen version list for the reproducibility statement.

steps.title: Verify KEEL loader and inventory datasets
steps.description: Load every bundled KEEL binary dataset and record n, d, imbalance ratio, minority count, nominal features and missing values. If the package fails, request network access to the KEEL website instead.

steps.title: Search prior matching-based resampling work
steps.description: Use the literature-review skill with CrossRef, arXiv and web search to find prior uses of stable matching, assignment, roommates, optimal transport and statistical matching in undersampling or instance selection, and set evidence-backed novelty claims.

steps.title: Build verified reference base
steps.description: Collect and DOI-verify core references: undersampling methods, matching theory (deferred acceptance, rural hospitals theorem, stable roommates, Kuhn-Munkres, Edmonds, uniqueness results), optimal matching in observational studies, evaluation methodology, KEEL, imbalanced-learn, complexity measures; export references.bib.

steps.title: Write related-work synthesis and positioning
steps.description: Draft structured notes for the Introduction and Related Work sections, including a positioning table that compares the closest methods (NearMiss, cluster-based, StatMatch, OT undersampling) with the proposed family.

steps.title: Curate KEEL benchmark datasets
steps.description: Select ~50-60 binary datasets with at least 10 minority instances using documented inclusion rules; encode nominal features, handle missing values, and label each dataset's base-data family for the independence robustness check.

steps.title: Compute dataset characteristics and complexity
steps.description: Build the dataset table (n, d, IR, minority size) and compute data complexity measures (e.g. F1, N1, N3) plus the safe/borderline/rare/outlier minority typology for the later meta-analysis.

steps.title: Define fixed cross-validation folds
steps.description: Generate 5x5 repeated stratified folds per dataset with recorded seeds and save them, so every sampler and classifier sees identical splits.

steps.title: Implement four matching undersamplers
steps.description: Write imbalanced-learn-compatible samplers: boundary-stable (hospitals-residents deferred acceptance with minority capacities), boundary-optimal (rectangular min-cost assignment), coverage-stable (stable-roommates pairing, keep one per pair, iterate) and coverage-optimal (Edmonds min-weight matching on a kNN graph, iterate), with exact target counts and seeds.

steps.title: Prove and test theoretical properties
steps.description: Write proofs of greedy equivalence and uniqueness under distance-symmetric preferences, proposer invariance of the selected subset via the rural hospitals theorem, the ball characterization of the boundary-stable subset, and Wasserstein interpretations of the optimal variants. Unit-test each against reference solvers and brute force on tiny instances.

steps.title: Profile runtime and illustrate selections
steps.description: Measure runtime scaling with majority size, and draft Figure 1: a 2D synthetic panel showing which majority points each matching method, RUS, NearMiss and cluster centroids retain (figure-style skill).

steps.title: Build leakage-safe experiment runner
steps.description: Pipeline with scaling and resampling inside training folds only. Samplers: none, RUS, NearMiss-1/2/3, Tomek, ENN, NCR, OSS, CNN, IHT, ClusterCentroids, the 4 proposed methods, plus class weighting and SMOTE as references. Classifiers: CART, kNN, SVM-RBF, LR, RF with default settings. Logs per-fold metrics, selection diagnostics and runtimes, with checkpointing.

steps.title: Run main benchmark
steps.description: Run all datasets x 25 folds x samplers x classifiers in parallel on 32 cores, check completeness, and save the raw per-fold results as a parquet artifact. Primary metrics G-mean and ROC-AUC; secondary balanced accuracy, F1, MCC, PR-AUC, sensitivity, specificity.

steps.title: Run sensitivity and ablation experiments
steps.description: Vary the target ratio (1:1, 1:1.5, 1:2), the coverage keep-rule (random vs nearest-to-minority), the preference structure (Euclidean vs class-specific asymmetric) and the kNN candidate size, on all datasets with a reduced classifier set.

steps.title: Run rank-based omnibus and post-hoc tests
steps.description: For each classifier and primary metric: average ranks, Friedman/Iman-Davenport, Wilcoxon signed-rank with Holm correction for each proposed method vs each baseline, CD diagrams, and win/tie/loss counts.

steps.title: Run Bayesian and robustness analyses
steps.description: Bayesian signed-rank tests with a ROPE (proposed vs RUS and vs the best baseline); robustness checks with one dataset per family, IR groups (<9 vs >=9) and secondary metrics; export LaTeX tables and publication figures.

steps.title: Compute selection diagnostics
steps.description: For each sampler, quantify boundary proximity of the retained majority, Wasserstein/energy distance to the minority and to the full majority, and the share of noisy/borderline majority retained, mapped onto the boundary-vs-coverage desiderata.

steps.title: Analyse when matching helps
steps.description: Meta-regression of performance gains (proposed minus RUS and minus best baseline) on IR, size, dimensionality and complexity measures, with interpretable plots and a runtime comparison figure.

steps.title: Derive paper narrative and figure plan
steps.description: Run the paper-narrative skill on a draft abstract and the figure deck to fix the storyline and Figure 1, then finalize every figure with the figure-style skill.

steps.title: Draft LaTeX manuscript
steps.description: Write the elsarticle manuscript: Introduction, Related Work, Preliminaries, Methods (algorithms, propositions, proofs), Experimental Design, Results, Discussion with limitations, Conclusion, and supplementary material, with every number generated from the results files.

steps.title: Compile and verify manuscript
steps.description: Compile with tectonic in the latex environment, then cross-check every reported number, table and citation against the result artifacts and references.bib.

steps.title: Referee-style self-review and revision
steps.description: Write an internal referee report in your usual format (summary, assessment, numbered major and minor comments), revise the manuscript to address it, and deliver the final PDF and source bundle.

desired_outputs: Manuscript PDF plus LaTeX source bundle (elsarticle .tex, references.bib, figures)
Python module of the four matching undersamplers with unit tests
Curated KEEL dataset registry and dataset-characteristics table
Raw per-fold benchmark results (parquet) and summary tables
Statistical analysis tables and figures (CD diagrams, Bayesian tests, mechanism and runtime plots)
Internal referee-style review report of the draft

feasibility.rationale: Running the full study and drafting the paper is feasible on this machine; whether matching-based undersampling beats random undersampling is the open empirical question, and the manuscript will report the outcome either way. Exact Edmonds matching on the largest majority classes will run on a kNN-sparsified graph, which the paper will state.
